source_title: Live: Netanyahu alleges vote fraud, protesters urge Eisenkot to unite with Arabs
source_excerpt:
Israel Election 2026: Opposition bloc reaches deal to oust Knesset speaker
Israeli opposition parties have reportedly agreed to remove Knesset Speaker Amir Ohana when the new parliament convenes on November 10.
The bloc, which includes Arab-led parties, holds a majority in the 120-member Knesset. The Democrats leader Yair Golan said appointing a new speaker would be among its first moves after the parliament is sworn in.
Israel Election Results: Mossad to join probe into alleged election interference, report says
Israel’s Mossad spy agency is reportedly joining an investigation into suspected foreign interference in this week’s national election, with Qatar and Turkey among the countries under scrutiny, Channel 12 reported.
The probe, which also involves the Shin Bet, centres on allegations that Arab voters were paid to increase turnout on Tuesday. The Central Elections Committee has stressed that the investigation is limited in scope and that the election results are not in question.
Israel Election 2026: Netanyahu’s bloc leads with 53 seats, but neither side has Knesset majority
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu’s bloc secured 53 seats in the next Knesset, maintaining its lead after the final vote count was announced on Thursday, according to the Central Elections Committee. The opposition bloc won 48 seats, leaving both sides short of the 61 needed for a parliamentary majority. Arab parties secured a record 19 seats.
Israel Election Results: Netanyahu’s rivals hold talks with Ra’am as efforts to form alternative bloc continue
Leaders seeking to replace Benjamin Netanyahu held a series of meetings on Thursday, with some discussions involving the Ra’am party. Democrats chairman Yair Golan met separately with Ra’am chief Mansour Abbas, Yashar chairman Gadi Eisenkot and Yair Lapid. Meanwhile, B’Yachad chairman Naftali Bennett held talks with Eisenkot and Golan. (Jerusalem Post)
Israel Election Live: Eisenkot accuses Netanyahu of undermining legitimacy of Israel election results
Yashar party chairman Gadi Eisenkot accused Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu and his Likud party of seeking to cast doubt on the legitimacy of Israel’s election results. Meanwhile, Yair Lapid called for patience as political leaders continued behind-the-scenes negotiations to form the next government.
Israel Election Live: Polymarket probes suspicious bets on Netanyahu's election victory, says report
Prediction market platform Polymarket is investigating a series of unusually timed and profitable bets placed on Israel's parliamentary election, after hundreds of newly created accounts wagered on Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu retaining power shortly before voting ended, Bloomberg News reported on Thursday.
According to Bloomberg, the accounts placed bets on Tuesday, shortly before polls closed, predicting that Netanyahu would remain Prime Minister and his Likud party would win the highest number of seats.
The trades quickly turned profitable after some exit polls indicated that Likud had secured more seats than initially expected. Several accounts have already cashed out more than $100,000 collectively, while many other wallets are sitting on significant unrealised gains, the report said.
Polymarket's internal investigative team told Bloomberg that it was reviewing dozens of newly created wallets involved in election-related trading. Data analysis firms Polysights and Bubblemaps have also flagged the activity as suspicious and launched their own investigations, Bloomberg reported.
A Bubblemaps representative separately told Reuters that 101 Polymarket accounts were funded for the first time on election day, before polling ended.
"A few have already sold out for a profit after the exit polls," the representative told Reuters.
The episode comes amid growing scrutiny of prediction market platforms over possible insider trading. Polymarket and Kalshi have faced increased attention as trading volumes have surged and concerns over suspicious transactions have grown.
Reuters reported in May that Polymarket had recorded a significant increase in trades flagged as suspicious during the year.
Israel Election: Qatar denies interfering in Israeli elections, rejects funding allegations
Qatar on Thursday denied allegations that it had interfered in Israel's parliamentary elections or funded activities to influence the outcome, dismissing claims it said were being circulated by Israeli politicians and media outlets.
Qatari Foreign Ministry spokesperson Majed Al Ansari said in a statement posted on X that the accusations would not deter Doha from continuing its mediation efforts, along with its diplomatic and humanitarian work.
Doha maintained that the allegations were baseless and reiterated its commitment to its ongoing diplomatic engagements.
Israel Election Deadlock: Eisenkot vows to push key campaign pledges despite uncertainty over coalition
Opposition leader Gadi Eisenkot has vowed to move ahead with key campaign promises once Israel's next Knesset is sworn in on November 10, despite uncertainty over his prospects of forming a governing coalition.
According to The Times of Israel, Eisenkot said his centrist Yashar party was already preparing legislation on four key issues: introducing universal military and national service, setting up a state commission of enquiry into the October 7 massacre, reforming the state budget mechanism and prioritising Israelis who serve.
He said the proposed measures would be brought to a vote after the new Knesset is sworn in, in coordination with his political partners.
Eisenkot's announcement comes as the political deadlock following Israel's parliamentary election leaves the formation of the next government uncertain.
Israel Election 2026: Protesters urge Netanyahu's rival to form Jewish-Arab coalition
Israeli left-wing activists gathered outside the home of Gadi Eisenkot, Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's main political rival, on Thursday, urging him to explore forming a government with the support of Arab parties. The protesters called on Eisenkot to break with parties ruling out any alliance with Arab representatives and consider a Jewish-Arab coalition.
Einat Keren, an Israeli citizen who attended the demonstration, said protesters wanted Eisenkot to cooperate with representatives of Arab parties because they believed those parties deserved a place in the government.
"We hate the fact that so many of our parties are just saying we will never sit with the Arab parties," she said.
Amir Badran, deputy mayor of Tel Aviv-Jaffa, called on Eisenkot to show the political courage to work with Arab parties and lead the formation of a different government. "Be brave enough to do it because this is what the people of Israel need, this is what Palestinians need," he said.
Israel has completed counting votes in its October 27 parliamentary election, but the results leave Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's bloc short of a majority in the 120-member Knesset. With all votes counted, Netanyahu's bloc secured 53 seats, compared with 48 for the opposition and 19 for Arab parties, Israeli media reported on Thursday.
The outcome leaves no political bloc with the 61 seats needed for a parliamentary majority, setting the stage for potentially difficult coalition negotiations. Netanyahu's Likud emerged as the largest party, winning 27 seats, but its position does not guarantee that he can form the next government.
